body:
@Mulgikapsas I think we've had similar issues before, I'm sorry but I don't see it as a bug. `@PermitAll` does not mean that an invalid token can be sent along the way.
What is the use case ?
@sberyozkin Prometheus is supplying JWT token when scraping /metrics page. I would like Authorization header to be ignored as there is no security on /metrics or /health endpoints by default.

@Mulgikapsas OK, thanks. 
Here is another scenario: the user code would like to access `JsonWebToken` in the `@PermitAll` method, irrespective of what the token `groups` claim is set to. The policy configuration in your case should work on the `@PermitAll` if there is no token, but I don't think we can just dismiss the available token based on the fact it is a `permit` policy.

Can you configure Prometheus to not send the tokens or make it sending the valid tokens, why are those tokens invalid ?

Otherwise we'd need to make some code concessions to support the cases where the tokens are not meant to be sent :-). For example 1) have the in-scope policy info available to HttpAuthenticators 2) have a new policy mode, like `ignore-credentials` 3) update all HttpAuthenticators to check the current path, and if it is `ignore-credentials` and the path matches then we skip the creds validation

This will add to the processing time and we will do it all to accommodate the tools/some client code which post the invalid credentilals :-)

Can you please check what can be done at the Prometheus level ?

CC @stuartwdouglas

Basically at the moment we do pro active authentication, so if there is a credential there we will attempt to verify it, and actively block invalid credentials even if the resource is unprotected. 

I think we can do this by simply having a setting that ignores auth failure and lets the request proceed. If the request does not require security then it will work as expected, if it does then the failed security check will force a challenge to be sent and valid credentials can be supplied.

@stuartwdouglas indeed, on the secure path it would fail anyway, good point. Should we just have a new policy mode, `permit-and-ignore-authentication`, a bit long but is clear what it is ? Or something shorter may be...

@Mulgikapsas Yes, you can use JWK key set, for example, see this [test resource](https://github.com/smallrye/smallrye-jwt/blob/master/testsuite/basic/src/test/resources/publicKeySet.jwk). Make sure the token `kid` header matches one of the keys. Search for `PEM to JWK` online converter to get this set prepared quickly.
In Wildfly/Undertow this is called proactive-auth, so `quarkus.http.proactive-auth=false` would be my preference to turn it off.
Sounds good, we can just update the docs and say it applies to the `permit` policies

Are there any plans to introduce quarkus.http.proactive-auth propery?

@sberyozkin The "kid" header is missing from the token supplied by Prometheus but is present on the other tokens.

@sberyozkin @stuartwdouglas 
I am currently looking to contribute here also.

Besides adding `quarkus.http.proactive-auth` option (quite simple in `io.quarkus.vertx.http.runtime.HttpConfiguration`), looking into the following call stack I am considering altering the behaviour in `QuarkusIdentityProviderManagerImpl`.
Or even in `IdentityProviderManagerCreator` that builds it.

But this would need adding into `quarkus-security` a dependency to `quarkus-verx-http`.
Would that be alright❓
